Total-plus-allocation count models

Source: R/countreg_alloc.R
countreg_alloc.Rd

Fits a joint model of a total count and its allocation across categories, such as the number of crashes at a site and their split by severity (ordered categories) or by crash type (unordered categories). The total follows any count family of the package (with covariates in its mean and distribution parameters). The split follows an ordered probit or ordered logit model for ordered categories, with covariates in the propensity and in the thresholds (generalized thresholds), or a multinomial logit model (link = "mnl") for unordered categories, with covariates whose effects differ by category.

Usage

countreg_alloc(
  formula,
  data,
  family = "NB2",
  alloc_formula = NULL,
  threshold_formula = ~1,
  link = c("ordered_probit", "ordered_logit", "mnl"),
  likelihood = c("multinomial", "fractional"),
  dis_param_formula_1 = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_2 = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  truncated = FALSE,
  group_var = NULL,
  stderr = NULL,
  method = "BFGS",
  max.iters = 1000,
  start.vals = NULL,
  ndraws = 1500,
  engine = "quadrature",
  verbose = FALSE,
  rpar_total = NULL,
  rpar_alloc = NULL,
  rpar_threshold = NULL,
  correlation = c("none", "within", "across"),
  rpar_draws = 500,
  seed = NULL,
  shared_formula = NULL,
  shared_in = c("total", "alloc"),
  shared_nodes = 20,
  .setup_only = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

a formula with the category counts on the left, as cbind(cat_1, ..., cat_J), and the total's mean model on the right. For the ordered links the columns go from the lowest to the highest category; for "mnl" the first column is the base category and the order of the others does not matter. The total is the sum of the categories. An offset() term (an exposure) belongs here.

data

a data frame.

family

the count family of the total (see countreg()), or a family made with new_count_family().

alloc_formula

a one-sided formula for the allocation propensity. By default the right-hand side of formula without its offsets. For the ordered links its intercept is dropped (the thresholds absorb it).

threshold_formula

a one-sided formula for the thresholds of the ordered links (generalized thresholds). Default ~ 1, fixed thresholds. It must have an intercept.

link

"ordered_probit" (default) or "ordered_logit" for ordered categories such as severity levels; "mnl" (multinomial logit) for unordered categories such as crash types, collision types or vehicle types. See Details.

likelihood

"multinomial" (default) or "fractional"; see Details.

dis_param_formula_1, dis_param_formula_2

formulas for the total's distribution parameters, as in countreg().

offset

optional names of offset columns (log scale), instead of offset() in formula.

weights

optional frequency weights: a column name or a numeric vector.

truncated

TRUE when the data contain only units with a positive total (for example data built from crash records): the total then follows the zero-truncated distribution \(P(c) / (1 - P(0))\).

group_var

optional column naming the units for cluster-robust standard errors (such as a site observed over several years).

stderr

"normal" (from the Hessian), "robust" (sandwich) or "cluster" (sandwich by group_var). The default is "normal" for the multinomial likelihood and "cluster" (or "robust" without group_var) for the fractional one, whose Hessian alone does not give valid standard errors.

method, max.iters, start.vals, verbose

optimizer settings, as in countreg().

ndraws, engine

integration settings of families without a closed form, as in countreg().

rpar_total, rpar_alloc, rpar_threshold

one-sided formulas of random parameters in the total's mean, the allocation propensity and the gaps between thresholds. The intercept is random only when the formula has the term 1 itself (~ 1, ~ 1 + x; ~ x makes only the slope random). Each term adds a normal random deviation, with mean zero, to the corresponding coefficient, so the coefficient in the equation's own formula is the mean (~ 1 in rpar_alloc is a random intercept of the propensity, even though its fixed intercept is absorbed by the thresholds). rpar_threshold shifts the log gaps of all thresholds above the first by one common random amount, so it changes the share of the middle categories (a common shift of all thresholds would be the same as a random propensity intercept). For link = "mnl", rpar_alloc gives each category but the first its own random coefficients. The random coefficients are drawn once per unit of group_var (shared by all its rows, such as the years of a site), or once per row without group_var.

correlation

correlation of the random parameters: "none" (independent), "within" (correlated within each equation) or "across" (correlated within and across the total and the allocation, which lets a unit's unobserved crash frequency and its severity propensity be correlated).

rpar_draws

the number of simulation draws per unit (randomly shifted Halton points, a separate block and shift for each unit).

seed

seed of the random shifts of the draws (stored in the fit, so predictions use the same draws); random by default.

shared_formula

optional one-sided formula of a shared site-year (row-level) random term: one standard normal draw \(u\) per row that enters each equation in shared_in with a loading \(s'\kappa_e\), where \(s\) are the variables of shared_formula (~ 1 for a constant loading) and \(\kappa_e\) its coefficients in equation \(e\). It correlates a row's total with its split (the term \(\eta_{it}\) of Shabab et al. 2026); see Details.

shared_in

the equations the shared term enters: any of "total" (the log mean), "alloc" (the propensity; for "mnl", each category but the first) and "threshold" (the log gaps between thresholds). Default c("total", "alloc").

shared_nodes

the number of Gauss-Hermite nodes for the integral over the shared term of each row. After the fit, the log-likelihood is recomputed with twice the nodes, with a warning if it changes by more than 0.05 (large loadings, above about 1 in the total, can need 40 or more nodes).

.setup_only

internal use: return the model setup without fitting.

Value

An object of class "countreg_alloc", with methods coef(), vcov(), logLik(), summary(), predict(), fitted(), simulate(), tidy(), glance() and confint().

Details

The two parts. With \(c = \sum_j y_j\) the total, the multinomial likelihood of a unit is $$P(c) \frac{c!}{\prod_j y_j!} \prod_j \pi_j^{y_j},$$ the probability of the total times the multinomial probability of its split. This is a proper joint likelihood of the category counts, so likelihood-ratio tests, AIC and BIC are valid, and so are simulation and prediction intervals. With a Poisson total the categories are independent Poisson counts with means \(\mu \pi_j\); with an NB2 total they are negative multinomial.

Zero totals are part of the model. The total's distribution includes zero. A unit with no events contributes \(P(c = 0)\) and nothing about the split, because a zero total has no shares. The total is not truncated at one: the indicator \(\omega\) of Shabab et al. (2026), which switches off the allocation term for zero totals, does the same thing. Only when the data hold units with at least one event by construction should truncated = TRUE be used; fitting such data with the untruncated total biases the count model, and countreg_alloc() says so when it sees no zero totals.

Fractional likelihood. likelihood = "fractional" raises \(\pi_j\) to the observed share \(y_j / c\) instead of the count, as in Shabab et al. (2026). A unit with one event then carries the same weight in the split as a unit with a thousand. This is a quasi-likelihood: the estimates are consistent, but standard errors must come from the sandwich (the default), and likelihood-ratio tests, AIC and BIC are not available.

Unordered categories. With link = "mnl" the categories are types with no order (crash types, collision types, vehicle types) and \(\pi_j = \exp(z'\delta_j) / \sum_k \exp(z'\delta_k)\), with \(\delta_1 = 0\) for the first category (the base). Each other category has its own coefficients, named Allocation[<category>]:, the effects on the log odds of that category against the base; a different base gives the same fit. With a Poisson total and the count model's covariates in alloc_formula, the model is the same as independent Poisson regressions of the categories; with an overdispersed total (such as NB2) the categories share the total's unobserved heterogeneity. The split assumes independence of irrelevant alternatives; random coefficients in rpar_alloc (one set for each category but the first) relax it. The threshold options (threshold_formula, rpar_threshold, shared_in = "threshold") are for the ordered links only.

Thresholds. For the ordered links the thresholds are \(\psi_1 = v'\theta_1\) and \(\psi_k = \psi_{k-1} + \exp(v'\theta_k)\), which keeps them ordered for every \(v\). The coefficients Threshold1: are on the scale of the latent propensity and Threshold<k>: (k >= 2) on the log scale of the gap between thresholds.

Random parameters. With rpar_total, rpar_alloc or rpar_threshold, the likelihood of a unit is the average over rpar_draws draws of its coefficients of the product of its rows' likelihoods (maximum simulated likelihood), with analytic gradients. The random coefficients are \(b = L u\), with \(u\) standard normal and \(L\) lower triangular; its elements are reported as sd: (the diagonal) and chol: (below the diagonal), and summary() shows the implied standard deviations and correlations. With the fractional likelihood the integrand is the product of the rows' quasi-likelihoods, as in Shabab et al. (2026).

Shared site-year term. Random parameters drawn per unit of group_var are shared by all the rows (years) of the unit. A row's own total and split can also share an unobserved factor: shared_formula adds \(\lambda_{e,it} u_{it}\) to each equation \(e\) in shared_in, with \(u_{it}\) standard normal and drawn anew for each row, and loading \(\lambda_{e,it} = s_{it}'\kappa_e\). The covariance of the term in two equations is \(\lambda_{e}\lambda_{e'}\): equal signs of the loadings mean that a site-year with more events than expected also has a more severe split (with the ordered links), opposite signs a less severe one. Changing the signs of all loadings gives the same model, so only their relative signs are identified. Shabab et al. (2026) use one loading for all equations, \(\eta_{it} = k's_{it}\), so their correlation is always positive; separate loadings include that model and allow a negative one. The integral over \(u_{it}\) is computed by Gauss-Hermite quadrature within each draw of the unit's random parameters, adapted to each row (the nodes are centred and scaled at the row's posterior mean and standard deviation of \(u_{it}\)). A shared term in the total also adds overdispersion to it, so with a family that has its own dispersion parameter (such as NB2) the two compete and can be weakly identified. With truncated = TRUE the row's likelihood is divided by its marginal probability of a positive total, \(\int (1 - P_0(u))\,\phi(u)\,du\), as the selection on a positive total happens after \(u_{it}\) is drawn.

Time-varying effects (tv()) can be used in every formula.

References

Shabab, K. R., Bhowmik, T., Zaki, M. H. and Eluru, N. (2026). A joint count and generalized ordered fractional split approach for addressing temporal instability in road safety analysis. Analytic Methods in Accident Research, 51, 100440.

See also

predict.countreg_alloc(), countreg(), negmultinom()

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
w <- washington_roads
# Ordered categories: crashes by severity
w$pdo <- w$Total_crashes - w$Injury_crashes - w$Fatal_crashes
m <- countreg_alloc(cbind(pdo, Injury_crashes, Fatal_crashes) ~ lnaadt +
                      offset(lnlength), alloc_formula = ~ speed50,
                    data = w, family = "NB2")
summary(m)
#> Total-plus-allocation count model
#> 
#> Total:       NB2 
#> Allocation:  ordered_probit with multinomial likelihood
#> Categories:  pdo < Injury_crashes < Fatal_crashes 
#> Units:      1501 (1101 with a zero total)
#> Std. errors: normal 
#> 
#> Total:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept) -9.38253    0.45195  -20.76   <2e-16 ***
#> lnaadt       1.16464    0.05252   22.18   <2e-16 ***
#> 
#> Distribution:
#>           Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> ln(alpha)  -0.7771     0.2133  -3.644 0.000269 ***
#> 
#> Allocation:
#>                    Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
#> Allocation:speed50  -0.3610     0.1932  -1.868   0.0617 .
#> 
#> Thresholds:
#>                        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> Threshold1:(Intercept)  1.28728    0.07255  17.743   <2e-16 ***
#> Threshold2:(Intercept)  0.10665    0.14192   0.751    0.452    
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -1294.2632  AIC: 2600.5263  BIC: 2632.4097 
head(predict(m))
#>         pdo Injury_crashes Fatal_crashes
#> 1 1.1768124     0.05791328   0.003570153
#> 2 1.0399738     0.05117918   0.003155019
#> 3 1.7241671     0.08484969   0.005230689
#> 4 0.3831482     0.01885549   0.001162375
#> 5 1.2315479     0.06060692   0.003736206
#> 6 0.5747224     0.02828323   0.001743563
# Unordered categories: crashes by type, other crashes as the base
w$other <- w$Total_crashes - w$Animal - w$Rollover
mt <- countreg_alloc(cbind(other, Animal, Rollover) ~ lnaadt +
                       offset(lnlength), alloc_formula = ~ lnaadt,
                     link = "mnl", data = w, family = "NB2")
summary(mt)
#> Total-plus-allocation count model
#> 
#> Total:       NB2 
#> Allocation:  mnl with multinomial likelihood
#> Categories:  other, Animal, Rollover (unordered; base: other )
#> Units:      1501 (1101 with a zero total)
#> Std. errors: normal 
#> 
#> Total:

#> lnaadt       1.16465    0.05252   22.18   <2e-16 ***
#> 
#> Distribution:
#>           Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> ln(alpha)  -0.7772     0.2133  -3.644 0.000269 ***
#> 
#> Allocation:
#>                                   Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
#> Allocation[Animal]:(Intercept)   -0.003171   1.046819  -0.003  0.99758

#> Allocation[Rollover]:(Intercept)  1.607992   1.647893   0.976  0.32917

#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -1408.7772  AIC: 2831.5545  BIC: 2868.7517 
predict(mt, newdata = w[c(1, 50, 200), ], type = "prob")
